SnowReport.Report:
Morning Report, 7:02 AM

Good Morning, Sugarloafers

It feels so good to be back in the swing of things, with the lifts turning, so many familiar faces around, and a little bit of lift-served adrenaline. It's looking like an even better day 2 all around, with another day of grooming on the trails and no need for a squeegee for your goggles.

Speaking of grooming, all of our open terrain is getting a touch up this morning, including Upper Narrow Gauge, Gin Pole, Sluice, and Lower Winter's Way. The cats got out after temps dipped last night, ensuring the best conditions for today. Expect slightly firmer snow up high and softer snow similar to yesterday down low.

SuperQuad and Skyline will start turning at 8:30 this morning, with DRC on standby if needed. These are the only ways uphill this weekend, as uphill travel including walking and hiking is closed.

Top of Skyline is currently reporting 31°F with northeast winds 20-30 mph. Any precipitation should stop by first chair, leaving us with our first greybird day of the season. Temps are supposed to stay around freezing today- slightly above down at the base and slightly below up high.

Our snowmaking team is paying close attention, waiting for temps to drop slightly so they can get back to work up high. As soon as we can, we're looking to blanket Narrow Gauge from Gin Pole to Peavy with our eyes on Spillway if conditions allow.

The village is rapidly coming alive, with more and more dining and retail outlets open daily. Alongside the Narrow Gauge Food Court, Widowmaker, 45 North, D'Ellies, Coast, and the Bag, we're welcoming Eighty8 Donuts and Java Joes to the fold today, the perfect treat for that mid-morning break. For the full list of hours, head on over to the Dining quick link.

It's shaping up to be a good one, so dust off those skis, do a couple warmup stretches, and get on up to the hill.

See you on the hill,
Nathaniel

Last Updated: 11/28/2026 | 1:22PM


Is there anything better than Saturday laps? We sure can't think of much. Come spend the afternoon with us and see for yourself.

Today's lineup includes T2, Upper Sunday Punch, and Lower Sunday Punch, all accessed via the Locke Mountain Triple from 8AM-3PM. Our grooming crew has been putting in the work, but it's still early season out there, so take it easy and keep an eye out for thin-cover areas.

Tonight, the groomers will be back out cleaning up today's turns and getting things dialed in for first chair at 8AM tomorrow.

Access today and tomorrow is open to New England Passholders, Ikon Passholders, Mountain Collective Passholders, and Ticket Pack holders. Previously purchased lift tickets will also be honored, but daily tickets are sold out for the weekend. Park in Barker Basin, with overflow parking at South Ridge and resort shuttles connecting the two.

Not here to ski? The Chondola is spinning at South Ridge for complimentary scenic lift rides up to North Peak Lodge, where hot cocoa and cinnamon buns are waiting from 10AM-2PM.

Hungry? Sliders is serving up tableside Carbonara, Foggy Goggle has nachos, and Barker Bar has burgers, beers, and a front-row seat to the slopes. Not a bad way to spend a Saturday.

We've also got a full slate of events to keep things rolling, including live music with Brad Hooper at Barker Bar, trivia at the Foggy Goggle, Family-Friendly Movie Night at the Grand Summit, and plenty more.

And before you head out, our Cyber Sale is still live, but the clock's ticking. Score up to 50% off select lift ticket days and up to 30% off lodging all winter long before the deals disappear. See you out there!

-Team Snow

SnowReport.Report:
The Snowmaking team was out in full force earlier this week, taking advantage of a prime weather window and continuing the push for winter. Over 400 guns ran at peak times, from the top of Upper Walking Boss to the bottom of Seven Brothers.

Unfortunately, Mother Nature doesn't always cooperate, and recent warm weather has temporarily put snowmaking on hold. Because of that, we are not quite ready for skiing and riding.

The good news? Colder temperatures are on the way. Forecasts call for snowmaking temps to return Monday night and into Tuesday, giving the team another solid window to fire up the guns.

We know everyone is waiting on Opening Day, and so are we. We don't have a date yet, and we're not going to guess. We expect a clearer picture after the weekend, and we'll share it here first.

In the meantime, we've got a weekend slate of entertainment lined up for you to get ready for the season. Stop by on Saturday for a Gondola Skyride, live music in the Bunyan Room, or to gear up for winter at Loon Mountain Sports.

Saturday Skyride

No skis required. In fact, no skis allowed. The White Mountain Express Gondola is scheduled to run Saturday, November 28, from 10:00am to 4:00pm. Pass holders can scan their pass to ride, and skyride tickets will be available at Guest Services. Saturday's weather looks cloudy with a chance of precipitation, and temperatures will be in the thirties. The Gondola will be open for foot traffic only, leave the skis and snowboards at home.

Gear Up for Winter

Loon Mountain Sports and The Bird are open Friday through Sunday, November 2729. Score up to 50% off top brands in store throughout the weekend. Details

We're Back in the Bunyan Room

The Paul Bunyan Room makes it's season debut this weekend. Head up for a cold one Friday through Sunday from 11:00am to 6:00pm. The Chris White Trio plays live Saturday at 1:00pm for some early season stoke. Mug Club members can renew for the season while they're there, which is an easy errand to run with live music on.

Thanks for your patience while we continue the push for Skiing and Riding. See you on the hill, soon.
